correctness.rationale: The sign identity and three-prime divisor-level factorization are exact. The nine-step coefficient recursion, explicitly enumerated, gives precisely 12 zero two-level sign configurations. Four-coin subset-sum coverage and fourteen checked extension inequalities prove all even two-level imbalances in [-3218,3218]. The 49-block induction proves every odd imbalance in [-K_a,K_a], and independent zero blocks inject 12 choices per new pair of levels; the support obstruction follows from sigma(n)/n<15/8 for odd numbers with at most two prime factors. The attached checker verifies the finite certificate and direct a=1,2 examples. These finite tests are not used as proof of the unbounded induction.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The published three-prime classification and Stewart criterion cover existence of such signed imbalances for this almost-practical family; the covered portion has expressly been excluded from the new contribution. The published exact two-prime Zumkeller bipartition count concerns even integers of form \(2^a p^b\), zero imbalance, and no 3-prime fixed-positive-imbalance multiplicity transfer. These do not imply the 12 independent zero blocks or the exponential lower bound.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existence of subset sums does not in itself imply a growing number of representations of the same sum: distinct-summand systems can be complete while a given target has one representation. Conversely, exact counts in a different two-prime zero-sum strip give no stated reduction to the present odd three-prime, all-fixed-odd-k family. The new proof supplies a disjoint-level injection with 12 choices per block; it does not rest on such an implication. Li full text remains inaccessible, so an implicit prior derivation is a residual risk.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equation \(\sum_{d\mid n} \varepsilon(d)d=k\) is exactly the two-way divisor partition with difference k and, equivalently, a subset of divisor sum \((\sigma(n)+k)/2\). The accessible Li abstract asserts infinitude for prescribed k, and the almost-practical framework implies existence, but neither inspected statement gives quantitative multiplicities of the exact subset-sum fibers. The new claim is not the existence reformulation.

value.rationale: The motivating new research studies existence of fixed divisor-partition imbalance and prime-support constraints. The result proves arbitrarily large multiplicities of the same prescribed odd difference along a ray with provably minimal distinct-prime support. An exact 12-way local zero-block supplies a structural amplification mechanism and a concrete exponent log(12)/log(49); unlike bare completeness or code novelty, this answers the natural quantitative partition-count question across all fixed odd target differences.
